transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I feel like I’m constantly bracing myself—my whole body stays tight all day from worrying about my husband and everything I’m juggling. It has just become so overwhelming lately, and I don't know how to relax anymore.
Did these worries and tension start after a specific stressful event or change in your life, or have you been this way most days even without one clear trigger? About how long has this been going on?

It really started about nine months ago when my husband was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and mild congestive heart failure, and I took on managing his care alongside all my community commitments. This constant, over-the-top worrying and feeling on edge has been going on almost every single day for about seven months now.

When your husband’s health or your responsibilities are calmer, do the worrying and physical tension still continue most days, or do they mainly flare up in response to those specific stresses? Also, are you worrying excessively about many other areas of life besides his care?

Yes, even during quiet moments when things should be calm—like when I'm trying to read a book—the tension and worry just don't stop. It has definitely spilled over into other areas, too, like worrying about letting people down at the art center or whether we'll have enough money to cover his changing medicine costs.

If your husband’s illness and caregiving demands were no longer a problem, do you think the excessive worry and physical tension would still be there most days? Or do they feel mainly tied to that specific stress?

Honestly, I think the worry has become so deeply ingrained by now that it would still be there most days, even if those caregiving demands were gone. It may have started with his health, but now my mind constantly jumps to worrying about our finances, letting people down at the art center, and everyday tasks. It just feels like this constant tension has taken over my whole life.

Along with the constant worry, have you also had symptoms like trouble sleeping, feeling restless or keyed up, getting tired easily, difficulty concentrating, irritability, or muscle tension? Which of these have been happening most days?

Yes, I constantly feel restless and keyed up, like I've had too much coffee, and my shoulders and neck are always incredibly tight and knotted. I also get exhausted so easily—feeling completely wrung out even after resting—and I struggle to concentrate on simple things like reading a book or following a conversation.

How much is this worry affecting your daily life—for example, your sleep, relationships, work, or ability to manage tasks? Has it made you cut back on activities or caused problems at home or in your community work?

It’s had a huge impact—I’ve actually started skipping or leaving early from my book club and art center planning sessions because I'm just too wound up and distracted to follow the conversations. At home, I’m falling behind on basic chores like laundry and paying bills on time. Even simple things like cooking dinner or tidying up feel like a massive effort because I feel so wrung out all the time.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes excessive, difficult-to-control worry occurring most days for about seven months, extending across multiple life domains beyond the original stressor, with associated restlessness, fatigue, poor concentration, and marked muscle tension. Symptoms persist even during calm periods and cause clear functional impairment in home and community activities, supporting generalized anxiety disorder rather than a purely stress-limited adjustment reaction.
